note: Adapted from the species description in Chhotani (1997), originally in English; the original describes only the soldier, records the alate as unknown and does not describe the worker or the nymph, so no body length or worker measurements are given. The Other section records only the nomenclatural history from the synonymy section of the original. Literature citations, figure numbers and distribution records are omitted.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Soldier: head capsule brownish yellow to pale brown; antennae brownish yellow; mandibles reddish brown; legs and abdomen paler. The whole head sparsely pilose. Head capsule subrectangular, sides nearly parallel and slightly diverging anteriorly, length to base of mandibles 1.26–1.66 mm, maximum width 0.83–0.97 mm. Antennae with 13 segments in all, of which segment 3 is the shortest. Clypeus trapezoidal. Labrum subpentagonal, distal end broad and rounded. Mandibles coarsely serrate, strongly incurved on the distal half, length 0.94–1.05 mm. Postmentum clavate, waist situated at the posterior third, length 0.70–1.01 mm; maximum width 0.27–0.32 mm, waist width 0.17–0.20 mm. Pronotum saddle-shaped; anterior margin emarginate, posterior margin nearly straight, length 0.30–0.38 mm, width 0.54–0.65 mm.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Other: the species name was first proposed as a nomen nudum by Chaudhry et al. in 1972 and described by Akhtar in 1974 on the basis of soldier specimens, the type specimen being a soldier.
